- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show upward trend bias, often starting from a flat or slightly rising baseline, then gradually increasing — but true outcomes frequently dip or stabilize earlier.
- After sharp spikes in history (e.g., 74.25, 76.67), model overshoots and continues rising, while true values often correct downward within 3–5 days.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in volatile periods — overestimates when history shows recent volatility or downward momentum.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the first 10 days of the 30d window, then gradually adjust — but true outcomes often show a sharper correction or reversal after the 15th day.
- Model underestimates low-price periods (e.g., 60s–65s) and overestimates high-price periods (e.g., 75s–80s), suggesting it misweights recent volatility or ignores supply/demand shocks.
- When history includes a recent low (e.g., 65–68), model often fails to recognize the “bottom” and continues upward — suggesting it lacks lagged correction logic.
- Forecasts are too smooth — fail to capture sudden drops or spikes in true outcomes, especially after a high or low in the last 5–7 days.
- Model tends to ignore short-term volatility and assumes linear continuation — true outcomes often show “reversal” or “reset” after a spike or trough.
- When true outcome is below 70, model often overestimates by 5–10 points — suggesting it lacks downward bias correction for low-price regimes.
- Model underestimates true outcomes when history includes a recent high (e.g., 75+), especially if followed by a drop — suggesting it fails to anticipate “pullback” or “correction” after peak.
